## Discussion

Existing computational tools for inferring multi-condition CCC largely rely on pseudobulking, a process that aggregates single-cell data into pre-defined clusters.
This approach relies on the accuracy of cell-type annotations and often fails to capture the continuous and multifaceted nature of cellular identities.
To address these limitations, CCC-RISE projects cells into eigen-states, or shared patterns of gene expression across conditions, and scores communication between eigen-states rather than annotated cell types.
Each cell is therefore represented by a continuous projection across all eigen-states, which allows researchers to map communication programs back onto individual cells based on their propensity to send or receive molecular signals.
By deriving eigen-states from transcriptional variation across conditions, CCC-RISE identifies signaling subpopulations with single-cell resolution, allowing researchers to infer communication patterns directly from the structure of their single-cell measurements irrespective of cell types.

While exploring the advantages of CCC-RISE through ALAD and IBD cohorts, we noted three distinct modes of interpretation that each defined different kinds of communicating populations through eigen-states.
First, ALAD component 6 defined an airway repair and fibrosis pathway among epithelial cells and was unique in its separation of divergent sender and receiver cells by component weight.
This separability allowed us to threshold the epithelial senders and receivers into groups characterized by distinct gene expression profiles, making CCC-RISE especially useful for identifying cases of paracrine signaling between cellular subpopulations.
In contrast, ALAD component 5 represented immune activation within a subpopulation of lymphocytes whose sender and receiver weights were collinear, suggesting homotypic signaling within a single group of cells.
Thus, ALAD components 5 and 6 represent two distinct modes of population-level communication that can be understood through differences in eigen-state interactions, with one describing non-overlapping sender and receiver eigen-states and the other describing homotypic signaling among a single eigen-state.
In a third mode of interpretation, IBD components 3 and 4 defined complementary hormone-secretion axes mediated by enteroendocrine (EE) sender cells.
However, unlike ALAD component 6, IBD component 3 and 4 sender weights did not effectively stratify EE cells.
We therefore characterized the cells based on their position along a spectrum between component 3- and component 4-like states, which were ultimately defined by distinct gene expression profiles and receiver cell targets.
This analysis was unique not only in its consideration of two components simultaneously but also in its evaluation of continuous, partially overlapping cell states.

Applied to the ALAD cohort, CCC-RISE demonstrated a distinct capacity to resolve communication at a subpopulation level, uncovering functional heterogeneity within canonical cell-type annotations that related to the underlying biology.
The airway repair and fibrosis pathway defined by ALAD component 6 was mediated by BTC--EGFR signaling between ciliated epithelial sender cells and basal and secretory epithelial receiver cells.
In healthy lung epithelium, BTC secreted by submucosal ciliated cells is known to initiate tissue repair upon binding EGFR and other growth factor receptors that are predominantly expressed on bronchial basal cells\ [@doi:10.1165/ajrcmb.20.5.3308].
In traumatized and damaged tissue, such as that of the lung allograft, these signals instead indicate problematic fibrogenesis\ [@doi:10.1038/ki.2012.43; @doi:10.3390/cells11060986].
The ability to distinguish these non-overlapping epithelial subpopulations within a single canonical "cell type" highlights CCC-RISE's capacity to identify communication patterns with more granularity than available labels.
Similarly, ALAD component 5 represented coordinated communication driving lymphocyte activation in a subpopulation of CD4+ T, CD8+ T, and NK cells.
Whereas the sender and receiver groups of component 6 were defined by differentially expressed genes, component 5's lymphocyte subpopulation was defined by co-varying expression of the component's top LR pairs, composed of a host of activating (GZMA, CCL4, CCL5, CCR4, CCR5, CD70, CD27, CXCL13, CD69, CD48, and CD244) and inhibitory (CLEC2D, KLRB1, and TIGIT) molecules.
Indeed, markers of immune cell activation are often co-expressed during states of heightened inflammation, and inhibitory markers tend to become upregulated during sustained lymphocyte activation, a protective phenomenon whose role is to dampen overactive immune responses\ [@doi:10.1136/lupus-2026-002068; @doi:10.1016/j.isci.2025.114551; @doi:10.1007/s10753-024-02045-y; @doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0030852].
In the context of lung transplants, this co-varying communication program likely points to inhibition that naturally follows activation rather than a profile of exhaustion, as increased CD8+ T cell activation and NK cell cytotoxicity have been observed during progression from ALAD to CLAD\ [@doi:10.1016/j.healun.2024.02.007].
Additionally, immune signaling is spatially graded and does not act uniformly over a population, which aligns with the continuously varying sender/receiver weights of activated lymphocytes identified by component 5\ [@doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004206].
These components thus show the interpretive advantage of CCC-RISE's single-cell resolution by dissecting classical cell types into more granular subpopulations, defined by raw gene expression and coordinated LR signaling rather than cell-type annotations of limited expressiveness.

A key goal of any multi-condition CCC-inference method is to identify communication programs associated with disease state by modeling the variation between samples.
In ALAD, CCC-RISE component 5 exhibited a significant stepwise association with six-month outcome, but the low statistical power of the dataset precluded our ability to make strong claims, leaving these findings hypothesis-generating.
The IBD dataset provided richness and statistical power beyond that of the ALAD data.
Here, CCC-RISE identified a complementary pair of hormone-communication programs among EE, enterochromaffin (EC), and tuft cells that was negatively associated with the shift from uninflamed to inflamed states in CD patients.
EE sender cells were spread continuously between villus- and crypt-like states, captured by components 3 and 4.
IBD is characterized by the infiltration of immune cells into the gut epithelium and the inflammation-driven death of otherwise healthy cells that ensues\ [@doi:10.1016/j.immuni.2023.01.002].
Indeed, the immune and epithelial cell-type abundances closely tracked inflammation status in the IBD data.
However, CCC-RISE further dissected these compositional trends, identifying villus-like EE cells as the specific subpopulation most sensitive to the inflammatory environment.
This finding recapitulates the spatial nature of the crypt-to-villus transition in the gut epithelium: as crypt cells differentiate, they migrate toward the gut lumen, thus becoming more exposed to external pressures such as inflammation\ [@doi:10.1016/j.cell.2018.12.029; @doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02634-7; @doi:10.1038/s41419-018-1275-5].
Through continuous, non-exclusive eigen-states, CCC-RISE resolved a particular population of hormone-secreting cells whose share of total EE cells decreased with patient inflammation severity.

Like CCC-RISE, Tensor-cell2cell and STACCato decompose a four-dimensional communication tensor to find signaling programs that vary across conditions\ [@doi:10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2; @doi:10.1016/j.ajhg.2026.05.005].
However, pseudobulk methods like these first annotate cell types on cells grouped across all conditions, thus removing between-condition variation in cell state before it can be used by the communication decomposition.
CCC-RISE instead maintains between-condition variation both while defining eigen-states and when decomposing communication programs.
Retaining this variation allows CCC-RISE to recover coordinated programs of LR pairs that pseudobulk methods either split across several programs or miss entirely.
Because eigen-states and cell types capture different structure from the same expression data, the programs identified by each method are not guaranteed to overlap\ [@doi:10.1016/j.cels.2025.101294].
Furthermore, re-annotating cells at a finer resolution caused pseudobulk methods to lose disease-associated programs, emphasizing the inconsistency of single-identity labels.
This loss suggests that condition effects act on cell states that cross annotation boundaries, so adding finer labels dilutes communication signals into groups too small to detect.
Conversely, when fit with more eigen-states, CCC-RISE largely preserved the programs found with fewer eigen-states, because each additional eigen-state captures a smaller source of variation than those before it\ [@doi:10.1016/j.cels.2025.101294].
As a result, CCC-RISE removes the dependence of communication findings on rigid cell-type labels and instead recovers coordinated signaling anchored to the largest sources of variation in the data.

Single-cell methods such as NICHES and Scriabin avoid labels altogether by scoring every cell pair, but the number of pairs grows quadratically, and each score inherits the sparsity and stochasticity of single-cell expression\ [@doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btac775; @doi:10.1038/s41587-023-01782-z].
For large datasets, this quadratic growth quickly becomes computationally intractable, so both methods rely on approximation techniques.
NICHES scores each cell's ligand or receptor expression against the average expression of its partner across the cell's sample, and Scriabin discovers interaction programs from cell--cell interaction matrices built on repeated subsamples of cells.
We found that this subsampling makes Scriabin's interaction programs unstable across random seeds.
Because eigen-states capture only the dominant patterns of gene expression shared across conditions, they largely exclude noise specific to individual cells\ [@doi:10.1016/j.cels.2025.101294].
Furthermore, the communication tensor grows with the number of eigen-states rather than cells, allowing CCC-RISE to scale to large multi-condition cohorts.
Despite this abstraction from raw expression, CCC-RISE populations agreed more closely with the expression-based NICHES scores than populations defined by annotated labels.
Together, this suggests that a continuous representation of cell state matters more than proximity to raw expression, allowing CCC-RISE to approach single-cell resolution without the computational and statistical costs of scoring every cell pair.

Although RISE's eigen-states enable CCC-RISE to perform tensor decomposition while retaining single-cell resolution, the method remains subject to limitations inherent to tensor decomposition techniques and transcriptomic inference.
First, RISE drastically reduces the number of hyperparameters relative to classical cell-type annotation pipelines, but researchers must still select both the RISE rank (number of eigen-states) and the CPD rank when constructing CCC-RISE models\ [@doi:10.1038/s41576-018-0088-9].
Here, we show that while rank selection is a challenging, empirical process, it can be aided by held-out prediction such as bi-cross-validation, resampling such as the jackknife, and fit-to-fit stability and collinearity\ [@doi:10.1214/08-AOAS227; @{doi:10.1016/S0169-7439(02)00090-4}; @{doi:10.1002/1099-128X(200005/06)14:3<229::AID-CEM587>3.0.CO;2-N}; @doi:10.1002/cem.801].
Additionally, like other transcriptomic CCC methods, CCC-RISE scores only the LR pairs cataloged in curated resources such as CellChatDB, so it cannot discover new interactions, and its results depend on the exact LR interactions documented in the chosen database\ [@doi:10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9; @doi:10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0].
CCC-RISE also assumes that gene expression is a sufficiently accurate proxy for protein abundance and functional interaction.
Because post-transcriptional regulation and binding kinetics can decouple mRNA levels from functional protein interactions, the communication patterns identified should be interpreted as hypotheses requiring experimental validation\ [@doi:10.1093/bib/bbaf280; @doi:10.1038/s41598-019-40939-2].
Finally, available validation approaches for CCC models remain limited.
For example, simulators such as SERGIO attempt to define a ground-truth transcriptomic signal but fail to accurately represent the structure of real biological data\ [@doi:10.1016/j.cels.2020.08.003; @doi:10.1186/s13059-023-02904-1].
Additionally, comparisons against prior knowledge, such as the NicheNet database, are limited by references that are incomplete or biased in construction\ [@doi:10.1038/s41592-019-0667-5; @doi:10.1038/s41596-024-01121-9].
Emerging technologies like single-cell proteomics and spatial transcriptomics, together with CCC models that constrain signaling by physical proximity, will be crucial to improve both the capture and validation of molecular signaling\ [@doi:10.1038/s41592-025-02620-7; @doi:10.1016/j.xgen.2025.100973; @doi:10.1038/s41592-022-01728-4].

In summary, CCC-RISE provides an unbiased framework for investigating CCC across multiple conditions at single-cell resolution.
By integrating the cell-alignment capabilities of RISE with the pattern-finding benefits of tensor-based CCC-inference methods, CCC-RISE reveals context-specific communication programs that are directly interpretable at the level of individual cells.
As single-cell, multi-condition studies become increasingly common, CCC-RISE will serve as a powerful tool to unravel the complex cellular dialogues that underpin disease.
Understanding CCC will rely on high-level analysis tools like CCC-RISE to map the entire landscape of potential interactions in an unbiased way, followed by targeted experiments to confirm which of these predicted pathways are functionally important.
